why: Decision 118: the player ships its engine rather than downloading it on first
use. The upstream project keeps thirty days of builds, so a pinned URL is a
time bomb - the first installation attempted a month later would 404, and a
checksum that cannot be fetched cannot be verified.
Each platform gets its own pin, its own digests and its own run on real
hardware before it appears here: an entry nobody has executed would be a
claim, not a pin. Windows has been run since V3.3.0; the macOS entry was
added on 22 September 2026 for V3.3.4 and is **not yet verified** - it is a
pin, and the run that makes it a claim is the first one on the Mac.
Which engine, and why these two. Both are LGPL builds of a current mpv with
libplacebo, so the renderer is gpu-next on both platforms and the codec
generation matches: the macOS pin carries FFmpeg 8.1.2, the same version the
server downloads for conversion, and the Windows pin carries an FFmpeg of
the same libavcodec generation (62.x). An earlier macOS candidate -
media-kit/libmpv-darwin-build v0.7.3 - was measured and refused: it builds
mpv 0.36.0 with FFmpeg 6.0 and `libplacebo=disabled`, so it has no gpu-next
at all, and the binary still carries the build machine's /nix/store paths in

verified: d3d11va decoding and gpu-next rendering into our own window, 0 dropped frames
WASAPI passthrough requested, refused by this machine's endpoint, PCM fallback
the library loaded from beside the executable, and from THEIA_LIBMPV

darwin/arm64.layout: lib/*.dylib beside each other, every dependency's licence text in licenses/, headers in include/mpv/
verified: the archive's SHA-256 matches the one the release page advertises, measured on 22 September 2026 before anything else was decided
the archive holds 19 dylibs and 11 symlinks, and every load command resolves to a sibling (@rpath/lib*.dylib) or to a system framework
the rpaths are @loader_path, @loader_path/../lib and @loader_path/../Frameworks - no build-machine path survives, which is what lets the libraries live in Theia.app/Contents/Frameworks

**on an Apple Silicon runner, 22 September 2026**: the fetch verified the archive and all 19 libraries by digest, and `mpv_render_context_create` succeeded with MPV_RENDER_API_TYPE_OPENGL and advanced control - the render path this pin was chosen for works

**and the film played**: 36 frames rendered by the host into its own NSOpenGLView, position advancing 0.00 to 9.29 s, `vo=libmpv`, `ao=coreaudio`, on a runner whose window session reported itself visible

the engine's own version string is `mpv v0.41.0-dev-gd97d68da9`, read from `mpv-version` on the runner - the release is *tagged* v0.41.4, and the tag is not the version. The same generation as the Windows pin (v0.41.0-1049), which is why the two platforms can be compared at all

what the runner could not answer: `hwdec=videotoolbox` was accepted and then refused by the machine - `[ffmpeg/video] h264: Failed setup for format videotoolbox_vld: hwaccel initialisation returned error`, which is what a virtualised runner without GPU-backed VideoToolbox does - and the film fell back to software decoding and played. Hardware decoding therefore needs a Mac, and the OSD over the film needs eyes
